subject: Hospitality
title: KFC and Global Localization
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: KFC and Global Localization.

hook.text: In Japan, KFC is Christmas dinner. Families pre-order weeks in advance. It's the country's biggest fast-food tradition.

buildup.text: Colonel Sanders franchised KFC in 1952 with a simple pitch: his secret recipe of 11 herbs and spices, cooked his way.

discovery.text: KFC adapts menus globally: rice bowls in Asia, spicy options in India, and beer in some European locations.

twist.text: KFC Japan's Christmas tradition started from a 1974 marketing campaign. 'Kurisumasu ni wa Kentakkii'—Christmas means Kentucky.

climax.text: Global fast food succeeds by being locally relevant. One brand, thousands of local adaptations—that's the real recipe.

punchline.text: Fried chicken for Christmas in Japan. Localization turns brands into traditions.

quiz.question: Why is KFC associated with Christmas in Japan?
options: A successful 1974 marketing campaign created the connection
